intro: In this lesson you'll describe people, places and things: a red car, a busy day, a very hot afternoon. In English the adjective comes before the noun, and after a person or thing you need am, is or are. Warm-up: describe your phone in two words, like 'It's new.'
teachingNotes: Indonesian puts the adjective after the noun (mobil merah); English puts it before (a red car). Common error: *'a car red'.
a/an and plurals: a/an goes before the adjective and follows the adjective's first sound (an old house, a new phone). Adjectives never take -s: two big bags, not *'two bigs bags'.

When the adjective comes after the person or thing, English needs be: She's tired, not *'She tired'. No 'a' before an adjective on its own: *'She is a tired'. The negative (isn't / aren't) is already known from a1-to-be.

very and really go before the adjective (very hot, really cheap, a very small room). Indonesian 'sekali' comes after (panas sekali), so learners may say *'hot very'. Only really goes before a verb: I really like it, not *'I very like it'.

Limits: no comparatives or superlatives (bigger, the biggest), no adjective order with three adjectives, no -ed/-ing adjectives, no past or future. Use verbs only with I/you/we/they (I like, we have); third-person -s isn't in this lesson's prerequisites. Avoid 'very' with strong adjectives like delicious or amazing.

keyPoints.title: Adjective before the noun
keyPoints.explanation: In English the adjective comes before the noun: a red car (mobil merah). a/an goes before the adjective, and the adjective never takes -s.

keyPoints.title: be + adjective
keyPoints.explanation: After a person or thing, use am/is/are + adjective: She's tired. Don't drop be, and don't put 'a' before the adjective alone.

keyPoints.title: very and really
keyPoints.explanation: Put very or really before the adjective to make it stronger: very hot, really cheap. Before a verb, use really, not very: I really like it.

assessment.prompt: Put the words in order: phone / I / new / a / have
assessment.rubric: Correct: I have a new phone. 'I have a phone new' = 30 (adjective after the noun).

assessment.prompt: Correct the mistake: It's a shirt blue.
assessment.rubric: Correct: It's a blue shirt. The adjective goes before the noun. 'It's blue shirt' (no a) = 70.

assessment.prompt: Correct the mistake: My sister tired today.
assessment.rubric: Correct: My sister is / My sister's tired today. Must add is. 'My sister is a tired today' = 40. 'My sister are tired' = 40.
Correct: The hotel is cheap (or inexpensive). Missing is ('The hotel cheap') = 30. 'The hotel is a cheap' = 40.

assessment.prompt: Correct the mistake: We very like the new teacher.
acceptableAnswers: we really like the new teacher
we like the new teacher very much
we like the new teacher a lot
assessment.rubric: Correct: We really like the new teacher. (We like the new teacher very much / a lot is also correct.) Keeping 'very like' = 0.

assessment.prompt: Translate into English: Jakarta sangat panas.
assessment.rubric: Correct: Jakarta is very / really hot. 'Jakarta is hot very' = 40. Missing is = 40. 'Jakarta is so hot' = 80.

blocks.text: Adjectives describe people, places and things: **big, small, new, old, cheap, expensive**. In Indonesian the adjective comes **after** the noun (*mobil merah*). In English it comes **before**: **a red car**.

id.text: Kata sifat menjelaskan orang, tempat dan benda: **big, small, new, old, cheap, expensive**. Dalam bahasa Indonesia kata sifat ada **setelah** kata benda (*mobil merah*). Dalam bahasa Inggris kata sifat ada **sebelum** kata benda: **a red car**.

rows.note: an, because old starts with a vowel sound

blocks.text: **a/an** goes before the adjective and follows its first sound: **a** new bag, **an** old bag. Adjectives never take **-s**: two **big bags**, not 'two bigs bags'.

id.text: **a/an** ada sebelum kata sifat dan mengikuti bunyi awal kata sifat itu: **a** new bag, **an** old bag. Kata sifat tidak pernah diberi **-s**: two **big bags**, bukan 'two bigs bags'.

blocks.explain: The adjective cheap goes before the noun bag, and it never takes -s.

id.explain: Kata sifat cheap ada sebelum kata benda bag, dan tidak pernah diberi -s.

blocks.text: An adjective can also come **after** the person or thing. Then English needs **am, is** or **are**: *Dia capek* = **She's tired**, never 'She tired'. Use the negative you already know: **The bus isn't full.**

id.text: Kata sifat juga bisa ada **setelah** orang atau benda. Dalam hal ini bahasa Inggris butuh **am, is** atau **are**: *Dia capek* = **She's tired**, bukan 'She tired'. Pakai bentuk negatif yang sudah kamu tahu: **The bus isn't full.**

blocks.text: Don't put **a** before an adjective on its own: **She is tired**, not 'She is a tired'. Use **a** only when a noun follows: **She is a tired teacher.**

id.text: Jangan taruh **a** sebelum kata sifat yang berdiri sendiri: **She is tired**, bukan 'She is a tired'. Pakai **a** hanya kalau ada kata benda setelahnya: **She is a tired teacher.**

blocks.explain: My phone = it, so the verb is is: My phone is old.

id.explain: My phone = it, jadi kata kerjanya is: My phone is old.

blocks.text: To make an adjective stronger, put **very** or **really** right **before** it: **very cold, really cheap**. With a noun, the order is **a + very + adjective + noun**: **a very small room**. Indonesian *sekali* comes after (*panas sekali*), but **very** always comes before.

id.text: Untuk menguatkan kata sifat, taruh **very** atau **really** tepat **sebelum** kata sifat: **very cold, really cheap**. Kalau ada kata benda, urutannya **a + very + kata sifat + kata benda**: **a very small room**. *Sekali* dalam bahasa Indonesia ada di belakang (*panas sekali*), tapi **very** selalu di depan.

blocks.text: Only **really** can go before a verb: **I really like it.** 'I very like it' is wrong. You can also say **I like it very much.**

id.text: Hanya **really** yang bisa ada sebelum kata kerja: **I really like it.** 'I very like it' salah. Kamu juga bisa bilang **I like it very much.**

blocks.explain: very goes right before the adjective: very big.

id.explain: very ada tepat sebelum kata sifat: very big.

id.title: Lebih kuat dengan very dan really

blocks.text: Many adjectives come in opposite pairs. Learn them together, then describe your room, your city or your office: *My office is small but very clean.*

id.text: Banyak kata sifat punya pasangan lawan kata. Pelajari bersama-sama, lalu deskripsikan kamarmu, kotamu atau kantormu: *My office is small but very clean.*

blocks.text: **old** is for people and things: an old man, an old phone. For people's age, **young** is the opposite: a young teacher.

id.text: **old** dipakai untuk orang dan benda: an old man (pria tua), an old phone (ponsel lama). Untuk usia orang, lawan katanya **young**: a young teacher (guru muda).

suggestedQuestions: Why does the adjective come before the noun in English?
When do I need is or are with an adjective?
What's the difference between very and really?
